title: Don't Outsource the Learning
summary: The article separates completing programming tasks from learning the concepts needed to supervise future work. Osmani recommends forming a hypothesis before requesting a fix, asking for explanations before code, reviewing suggestions and periodically reconstructing solutions without assistance. He uses existing research to motivate deliberate learning within ordinary AI-assisted development.
limitation: Practitioner synthesis of studies with different tasks and populations, including non-programming work; it does not establish long-term causal skill loss among software developers. Cited numerical findings were not independently rechecked here.

title: The Orchestration Tax
summary: Osmani describes the human cost of coordinating parallel coding agents as a limit on review and integration. He recommends matching the number of active tasks to review capacity, separating bounded background work from judgment-intensive problems, batching reviews and reserving uninterrupted time for difficult decisions. The goal is to improve accepted work rather than merely increase concurrent activity.
limitation: First-person operational guidance and a concurrency analogy, not a measured agent-scaling law or controlled productivity experiment. Suggested agent counts and percentage splits are illustrative.
topics: K:Human cognitive load; K:Review capacity and maintainers; K:Human-agent collaboration; K:Output versus shipped value

title: The Intent Debt
summary: The essay distinguishes missing recorded intent from complex code and missing human understanding. Osmani argues that an implementation cannot reliably recover why a consequential choice was made. He recommends keeping goals, constraints and decision rationale in specifications, repository instructions, lightweight decision logs and records of failures so future people and agents can use them.
limitation: Conceptual distinction and practitioner recommendations; no controlled evidence that recording these artifacts prevents drift, and generated explanations cannot establish historical intent.

title: The New Software Lifecycle
summary: Osmani comments on a Google whitepaper he coauthored, presenting coding agents as models surrounded by tools, context, controls and feedback. He distinguishes always-loaded from task-specific context and separates evaluation of final outputs from evaluation of execution paths. He argues that specification and verification become central constraints as implementation accelerates.
limitation: Author commentary on a coauthored whitepaper, not an independent empirical replication. The model-versus-harness proportions and reported benchmark improvements are illustrative or secondhand and are not repeated as validated measurements.

title: The Agent-Era Career
summary: Osmani’s career advice emphasizes choosing worthwhile problems, developing and demonstrating judgment, and retaining responsibility for delegated work. He recommends deliberate practice, explicit task boundaries, calibrated autonomy and careful completion beyond an agent’s initial draft. title: Earning taste and judgment
summary: Osmani argues that delegating routine coding can remove practice through which engineers develop judgment. He recommends deliberate code reading, recording agent mistakes, occasional unaided implementation, deep work in one system, and separate practice in specification and verification. The article connects these habits to career development while synthesizing other authors’ employment and cognition claims.
limitation: Career and learning guidance, with secondhand labor-market statistics and forecasts; no new employment estimate or controlled learning intervention. Numerical claims are not independently revalidated here.
